findings.title: The source remains named
findings.claim: The genitive names Allah as the source of the favor, and the later possessive suffix ties the signs to Him; the voyage's enabling gift and its signs stay in one named relation.
findings.mechanism: Niʿmat is constructed with Allah, while the suffix in āyātihi points back to the same named source. The proper name anchors both the means of passage and the signs being shown.
findings.reader_payoff: The movement is not detached from the favor and source named in the wording.
findings.containment: This follows the local genitive and possessive relations. It does not import disputed derivations of the divine name or claim that the verse names a natural mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The name, construct, and later suffix are supported by trusted local word analysis and resolved QAC alignment.

findings.title: Motion ordered toward showing
findings.claim: The purpose lām makes the ships' motion by favor serve the showing of some divine signs.
findings.mechanism: The lām governs the Form IV showing verb, linking the voyage to an intended disclosure rather than making the sign-reading an accidental lesson added afterward.
findings.reader_payoff: The purpose of the motion is audible in the clause itself.
findings.containment: The purpose clause states why the motion is presented here; it does not say every observer recognizes what is shown.

epistemic.reason: The purpose attachment and its governed verb are explicit in the trusted local analysis.

findings.title: Showing completes the seeing circuit
findings.claim: The Form IV verb presents God as making a plural audience see some of His signs, answering the opening summons to see.
findings.mechanism: The causative form turns seeing into something brought about for the audience; its -kum suffix names that plural audience, while min limits what is shown.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah moves from one addressed observer to a group made to perceive.
findings.containment: The plural suffix does not state that every person responds alike, and the partitive does not claim that all signs are shown.

epistemic.reason: The causative morphology, audience suffix, and partitive phrase are directly supported by trusted analysis and QAC alignment.

findings.title: A selected portion of signs
findings.claim: Min limits the shown content to some of His signs, so the maritime event is genuine evidence without exhausting the signs named as His.
findings.mechanism: The partitive preposition attaches to āyātihi and marks a portion from that larger set.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the ship scene as a real disclosure and as one selection within a wider reserve.
findings.containment: This bounds the content shown in this clause; it does not quantify the full set of signs or claim that only this portion is ever disclosed.

epistemic.reason: The preposition's attachment and partitive force are explicit in trusted local support.

findings.title: The first signs are His
findings.claim: The first plural sign phrase is explicitly possessed by God, presenting the markers as His rather than as free-floating data.
findings.mechanism: The suffix -hi attaches to āyāt and points back to Allah. The sign word can name a marker, evidence, verse, or portent, so the sea scene can be read as a meaningful unit.
findings.reader_payoff: The event is linked to a source and can be read, not merely observed.
findings.containment: The possessive marks the relation expressed by the wording; it does not exhaust what signs mean or make the natural event cease to be natural.

epistemic.reason: The attached possessive and the sign noun's local range are supported by trusted evidence.

findings.title: Observation becomes an asserted reading
findings.claim: After the ship scene is placed under perception, the independent inna clause emphatically asserts that signs are in the remembered event.
findings.mechanism: Anna introduces the content of seeing; inna opens a new main clause, and the later emphatic lām reinforces its delayed signs noun.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah shifts from asking the listener to see to affirming what the event contains.
findings.containment: The assertion interprets the scene as sign-bearing; it does not negate the ordinary fact of ship travel.

epistemic.reason: The embedded and independent particles and their local attachments are supported by trusted word analysis.

findings.title: Signs are found in the event
findings.claim: The repeated fi moves from ships in the sea to signs in the whole remembered phenomenon.
findings.mechanism: The first preposition marks the physical medium traversed by the ships; the second governs dhālik, letting the event itself become the setting in which signs are found.
findings.reader_payoff: The movement at sea becomes the location of an interpretation.
findings.containment: The second fi is an abstract relation in its clause, not a claim that the event is a literal container.

epistemic.reason: Both prepositional attachments appear in the trusted local analysis.

findings.title: One pointer gathers the scene
findings.claim: Dhālik points back across the ship, sea, favor, and showing sequence, holding that phenomenon together before the emphatic conclusion.
findings.mechanism: The distal demonstrative summarizes the preceding clause as one object of reflection; the following inna clause then states what is in it.
findings.reader_payoff: The conclusion receives a whole event rather than an isolated ship as its referent.
findings.containment: The demonstrative's range is the preceding scene in this ayah; no wider discourse reference is required.

epistemic.reason: The demonstrative's local antecedent and its position before the conclusion are directly supported.

findings.title: Emphasis reaches the delayed signs noun
findings.claim: The emphatic lām attached to āyāt reinforces the assertion that signs are present in the event.
findings.mechanism: The prefix is attached to the delayed noun inside the independent inna clause, so the asserted target arrives with emphasis.
findings.reader_payoff: The signs are not a passing afterthought to the scene.
findings.containment: The emphasis strengthens the clause without specifying a complete list of signs.

epistemic.reason: The prefix's attachment and distinction from the later benefactive lām are locally evidenced.

findings.title: The event holds multiple signs
findings.claim: After some of His signs are selected for showing, the emphatic conclusion presents signs in an indefinite plural within this event, allowing several aspects of the scene to be read as signs.
findings.mechanism: The earlier phrase has a possessive and partitive frame; the conclusion repeats the sign root without that suffix and locates the plural in dhālik.
findings.reader_payoff: Motion, medium, and favor can all remain visible as aspects of one sign-bearing event.
findings.containment: The plural is open within the event but is not an endless inventory, a count of all signs, or a guarantee that every observer reads them.

epistemic.reason: The grammatical shift is grounded, while the inference that several scene aspects become legible is bounded to this event.

findings.title: The opening question summons recognition
findings.claim: The negative question challenges the addressee to recognize the ships running; its force is not a denial that they run.
findings.mechanism: The question and negative particle frame the second-person seeing verb as a summons, while anna supplies the visible proposition being put before the addressee.
findings.reader_payoff: A familiar maritime event is treated as available evidence that deserves attention.
findings.containment: The rhetorical force does not remove the question form or claim that the addressee has already understood every sign.

epistemic.reason: The negative-question frame and its embedded proposition are described in trusted local support.

findings.title: The conclusion names its recipients
findings.claim: The final lām specifies the class for whom the signs are: each patient and grateful person.
findings.mechanism: The lām governs kulli ṣabbārin shakūrin, separating the purpose of divine showing from the human profile to which the concluding signs are directed.
findings.reader_payoff: The conclusion describes not only that signs exist but the kind of reader for whom they become legible.
findings.containment: The phrase qualifies reception; it does not say that others cannot see the ship.

epistemic.reason: The lām's attachment to the recipient phrase is explicit in the trusted evidence.

findings.title: Every member of a qualified class
findings.claim: Kulli distributes the signs to each individual, while the construct phrase limits that universal to the ṣabbār-shakūr profile.
findings.mechanism: The singular quantifier takes the patient-and-grateful descriptors as its class; the paired adjectives keep universality from becoming an undifferentiated claim about everyone.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees an individual path of reception repeated across the qualifying class.
findings.containment: This is a universal over the named profile, not over humanity without qualification.

epistemic.reason: The quantifier and its local construct complement are explicit; the root branch activation is checked against that phrase.

findings.title: Visibility and reception meet
findings.claim: Signs are offered broadly, but signhood becomes effective in a receiver described by endurance and gratitude: seeing can be physical while recognition takes sustained and responsive attention.
findings.mechanism: The opening summons seeing; the causative form distinguishes what is shown from the audience's uptake. The sign markers meet a universal quantifier restricted to the patient-and-grateful pair. The alternate small-input branch can be heard only as a form-distant image: a partitive selection of signs and a named favor make limited disclosure sufficient for recognition.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene can be visible without being equally interpreted; the closing profile describes a way of receiving what is shown.
findings.containment: The verse does not say that others cannot see the ships or that the signs are withheld. The limited-input image does not assert that a sign is literally small or that anyone physically grows. HFT links remain attributed because the reader identity is legacy_unbound.

epistemic.reason: The focus word coordinates and roots match QAC, but the integrated receiver mechanism comes from a legacy-unbound trace; its small-input branch remains a bounded attributed analogy.

findings.title: Favor as an unseen motive medium
findings.claim: The ship's motion by favor permits a form-distant image of favor as a continuing motive medium: an unseen enabling condition becomes visible through the passage it sustains.
findings.mechanism: The vessel supplies a concrete body, the running verb supplies ongoing movement, and the favor phrase binds that movement to an enabling good. A continuing-provision branch and a distant wind branch make a material force imaginable; the causative showing then exposes what motion alone can leave unnoticed.
findings.reader_payoff: The voyage can be pictured as carried by a benefit whose operation appears through its effects.
findings.containment: The verse does not lexically call favor a wind, name its direction or moisture, or exclude ordinary sailing conditions. Provision and wind are attributed, form-distant images; the literal motion and favor relation remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The trace coordinates and focus roots match the packet, but the continuing-provision and wind contacts are remote analogies from a legacy-unbound source.
